title: Welfare of Minor to be the Paramount Consideration — Section 13 HMGA

content.overview: Section 13 of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 provides that in the appointment or declaration of any guardian of a Hindu minor by a court, the welfare of the minor shall be the paramount consideration. No person shall be entitled to the guardianship by virtue of the Act or any law relating to guardianship in marriage among Hindus if the court is of opinion that his or her guardianship will not be for the welfare of the minor.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Court appointing/declaring guardian? (2) Welfare paramount? (3) Statutory natural guardian claim overridden if not for welfare?
content.study:
Section 13 is the controlling judicial standard. Even a person who is a natural guardian under s. 6 may be refused appointment/declaration if the court finds that the guardianship will not be for the minor’s welfare.

Welfare is a broad, fact-sensitive inquiry covering physical, emotional, educational and moral well-being.

No case holdings invented. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

sections.heading: Paramount consideration
sections.body: Welfare of the minor controls appointment or declaration of a guardian by the court.

sections.heading: Overrides mere statutory claim
sections.body: No entitlement under the Act or marriage-guardianship law if guardianship would not be for the minor’s welfare.

sections.heading: Scope of welfare
sections.body: Broad assessment of the minor’s overall well-being on the facts.

sections.heading: Link to s. 6
sections.body: s. 6 identifies natural guardians; s. 13 governs when the court decides.

sections.heading: Application
sections.body: Always end a guardianship problem with the welfare test when a court is involved.

provisions.title: Welfare of minor to be paramount consideration

examples.title: Natural guardian refused
examples.body: Father is natural guardian under s. 6 but court finds appointment not for the minor’s welfare — s. 13 bars entitlement.

hypotheticals.question: Can welfare displace the father as natural guardian in court proceedings?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. s. 13 provides that no person is entitled to guardianship if the court finds it would not be for the minor’s welfare.

distinctions.title: s. 13 welfare vs s. 6 natural order

misconceptions.trap: Natural guardian under s. 6 can never be refused by the court.
misconceptions.correction: s. 13 expressly allows refusal where guardianship would not be for the minor’s welfare.
